claim: For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb Z_2\) with \(\lambda\equiv3\pmod4\), the map \(f_\lambda(x)=x^2-\lambda\) has a unique globally attracting 2-cycle \(\alpha\leftrightarrow\beta\), where \(\alpha\equiv1\pmod4\) and \(\beta\equiv2\pmod4\). Every orbit enters \(B=\beta+8\mathbb Z_2\) after one iterate from an odd initial point or two from an even one. For \(y\in B\), set \(k_N(y)=\min\{N,v_2(y-\beta)\}\), \(d=N-k_N(y)\), and \(h_N(y)=0\) if \(d=0\), otherwise \(h_N(y)=2\lfloor d/3\rfloor+\mathbf{1}_{3\nmid d}\). This is the exact least additional time for \(y\bmod 2^N\) to enter the 2-cycle modulo \(2^N\). For every residue \(x\bmod2^N\), its least preperiod \(T_N(x)\) is zero if \(x\equiv\alpha\) or \(\beta\pmod{2^N}\); otherwise it is \(1+h_N(f_\lambda(x))\) when \(x\) is odd, it is \(1\) when \(x\) is even and \(f_\lambda(x)\equiv\alpha\pmod{2^N}\), and in all remaining even cases it is \(2+h_N(f_\lambda^2(x))\). The valuation increases exactly by three per two iterates after entry into \(B\).

correctness.rationale: For \(B=(1-\lambda)+8\mathbb Z_2\), \(g=f_\lambda^2\) maps \(B\) into itself and \(v_2(g(x)-g(y))\ge v_2(x-y)+3\). Banach contraction gives \(\beta\) and \(\alpha=f_\lambda(\beta)\). The exact expansions \(f_\lambda(\beta+u)-\alpha=u(2\beta+u)\) and \(g(\beta+u)-\beta=u[4\alpha\beta+(6\beta^2-2\lambda)u+4\beta u^2+u^3]\) give valuation increments \(k+2\) and \(k+3\). The tail-time law and the four-case finite-quotient formula follow by minimizing over the even and odd iterate times and handling the earlier time-zero/time-one cycle hits explicitly.

value.rationale: The result gives a pointwise exact least preperiod for every residue modulo \(2^N\), not merely a convergence bound. The exact valuation slope yields a sharp, parameter-uniform cost for resolving the attracting cycle to \(N\)-bit 2-adic precision. This is a natural finite-precision invariant for iterated p-adic maps and is strictly more informative than qualitative convergence or a nonsharp contraction bound.
